# Surfaces allowed to name an upstream command in an executable or directive
# context, one "<path>  <reason>" per line.
#
# bin/fm-fold-sweep.sh reports an allowlisted site as ALLOWED rather than hiding
# it, so a permitted dependency stays visible instead of disappearing.
#
# This file is deliberately near-empty. Per docs/capability-map.md, firstmate is
# transitional and its tools are NOT being renamed, so today every upstream name
# in bin/ is a legitimate live dependency rather than a migration leftover. The
# sweep is run to SEE that surface (8 sites for the quota record, 31 across both),
# not to enforce zero. Enforcement (--strict) becomes meaningful only if a
# custody artifact is ever actually adopted, which the capability map recommends
# against for these tools.

bin/fm-fold-sweep.sh  the sweep names every upstream command by definition
bin/fm-fold-lib.sh    manifest access reads upstreamCommand from fold.json
